patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea that began suddenly 2 hours ago. He reports eating reheated food from the afternoon, approximately 1 hour before symptom onset.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history. No known food allergies.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: College student living in dormitories. No recent travel history. Reports being in the middle of exam period and experiencing high stress levels.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, blood in stool, headache, or any urinary symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with symptoms of acute gastrointestinal illness.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Hello, doctor—about two hours ago I suddenly started having abdominal cramps with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. I think it may have been from reheated food I ate about an hour before it started, and it’s been happening since then.”
Have you had any fever or chills since the symptoms started?
“No fever or chills—I haven’t noticed any fever. It’s just the abdominal cramps with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea since it started.”
What type of food did you reheat and eat (for example, rice, pasta, meat, dairy, or pastries)?
“I reheated rice and some leftover meat, and I also had a little dairy with it. I ate it in the dorm right before the symptoms started.”
Did anyone else who ate the same food develop similar symptoms?
“Doctor, I’m not sure—only I ate that reheated food in my immediate area, but a couple of roommates mentioned stomach upset earlier today, though I don’t know the timing.”
Was the rice left sitting out at room temperature for several hours before it was refrigerated or reheated?
“No, it wasn’t sitting out for hours—I think it was refrigerated and then reheated pretty soon after. I just took it out, warmed it up, and ate it right there in the dorm.”
Have you noticed any blood in your stool, and are you experiencing frequent vomiting episodes or just nausea?
“No blood in my stool. I’m vomiting repeatedly—probably every few attempts to eat or drink—along with ongoing nausea and diarrhea.”
Where exactly are the abdominal cramps located, and are they constant or cramping/colicky in nature?
“Mostly around my lower abdomen, and the cramps come in waves—they feel crampy/colicky rather than constant.”
Are your symptoms starting to improve, staying the same, or getting worse since they began two hours ago?
“Honestly, doctor, I think it’s getting worse—the cramps are more intense and the vomiting and diarrhea are continuing, so I’m not really improving since they started about two hours ago.”
Are you having more vomiting than diarrhea, or are they roughly equal, and have you noticed any dizziness or visual disturbances?
“It feels like both vomiting and diarrhea are about equal, and I’ve been feeling a bit dizzy—no visual disturbances, just lightheaded.”
How long before you ate did your roommates become sick, and did they eat the same foods or different ones?

“I’m not totally sure about the timing—one roommate said they felt sick earlier today, but it wasn’t right around when I ate. I don’t know exactly what they ate, only that it was from the same dorm environment. I can’t confirm whether they ate the same reheated rice and leftover meat.”
Did you notice any metallic or unusual taste in the food, or are you experiencing any numbness or tingling around your mouth?
“No metallic or unusual taste, and I don’t have any numbness or tingling around my mouth. It’s mainly the abdominal cramps with the nausea, repeated vomiting, and diarrhea.”

“Doctor, the lightheadedness is making it hard to stand, and I feel like I can’t keep any fluids down. The cramps are getting more intense in waves, and the diarrhea keeps going along with the repeated vomiting. I’d like to know what you think it is and what I should do next.”

“Doctor, I’ve been lightheaded and it’s hard to stand. I can’t keep even small sips of fluids down—every time I try I end up vomiting again—and the diarrhea is continuing with worsening crampy, colicky waves.”
[DDX] Bacillus cereus food poisoning (emetic toxin), Staphylococcus aureus food poisoning, Viral gastroenteritis (Norovirus), Clostridium perfringens food poisoning, Salmonella enteritis
